lines.text: Think about driving to a friend's house. The map app gets you to the right street, fast.
But to park, you stop looking at the map and look at the curb. You measure the real thing.
Our robot does the same. Far away, it drives to the map's spot. Close up, its cameras find the tag.
A camera reports the tag relative to the robot. Something like: two meters ahead, ten centimeters left, and facing me.
The scoring spot is measured from the tag too: zero point six meters straight out of its face, turned to face it.
The robot only switches when it's sure: three photos have to agree first. We'll see how soon.
Chain those two arrows, and the robot knows where to stop, measured from the real element. The map's mistake drops out.
